$comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): every C99 6.7.4 `inline` form that DOES produce a definition in its own TU, in one program -- `static inline`, the GNU synonyms `static __inline` / `static __inline__`, `extern inline` (6.7.4p7's with-extern exemption), an `inline` PROTOTYPE beside a plain definition (6.7.4p7's quantifier is over ALL file-scope declarations, so one plain declaration restores the external definition), and a block-scope `inline` prototype (TF-C77's scope-symmetry rule: one specifier must not mean two things depending on where it is written). The exit code GATES ON THE VALUES, not on 'it compiled': 0 ->add_two-> 2 ->add_three-> 5 ->add_five-> 10 ->times_two-> 20 ->minus_one-> 19, +23 = 42, so a dropped body, a doubly-emitted one, or a mis-wired callee moves the exit code. The three spellings are pinned as SYNONYMS because they are -- MEASURED with `/usr/bin/clang -std=c99 -O0 -c` + `nm`, `inline int p(int){...}` and `__inline int p(int){...}` produce byte-identical symbol state; the C99-vs-GNU89 divergence rides the language mode and the `gnu_inline` attribute, never the spelling. The whole file is VERIFIED clang-clean (`-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -isysroot $(xcrun --show-sdk-path)`, zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang -O0 binary independently exits 42, so the expected exit code is ground truth from a real toolchain rather than merely what DSS happens to produce.
